svg.title: P023 · Chocolate or cookie products under 250
svg.desc: One row per qualifying chocolate or cookie product. IDs 1, 2 and 4 match, including uppercase CHOCOLATE. Tea Biscuit (ID 3) drops out. All three remaining sample prices pass. A price of exactly 250 would fail. ID 2 passes the first two filters, then drops out on its name. Cocoa Cookie (200) precedes Dark Bar (249). FROM Products · one table is enough. All three eligibility tests concern one catalogue item. Its subcategory, price and name can be checked together, and its own ID breaks a price tie.
svg.text: One row per qualifying chocolate or cookie product.
A sugar-free chocolate costs 150. Which of the three filters removes it?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.

g.aria-label: FROM Products · one table is enough
g.text: FROM Products · one table is enough
All three eligibility tests concern one catalogue item. Its subcategory, price and name can be checked together, and its
own ID breaks a price tie.

svg.text: IDs 1, 2 and 4 match, including uppercase CHOCOLATE. Tea Biscuit (ID 3) drops out.
All three remaining sample prices pass. A price of exactly 250 would fail.
Which name rule completes the shortlist?
ID 2 passes the first two filters, then drops out on its name. Cocoa Cookie (200) precedes Dark Bar (249).
AND Product NOT LIKE '%sugar-free%' / ORDER BY Sale_Price, ProductID
